description: The Inria Aerial Image Labeling dataset is a benchmark for automatic pixel-wise labelling of aerial imagery into two classes, building and not building. It covers 810 square kilometres of orthorectified colour aerial imagery at 0.3 m resolution, half for training and half for testing, with ground truth released only for the training part. Cities differ between the training and test subsets, from dense districts such as San Francisco's financial district to alpine towns such as Lienz in Austria, with Chicago, Kitsap County and Vienna among the samples, so that methods are judged on how well they generalise to new places. It was built from public domain imagery and official building footprints and introduced by Maggiori, Tarabalka, Charpiat and Alliez at IGARSS 2017. Coverage: selected U.S. and Austrian areas. Access: download after a form on the dataset page. Licence: public domain sources; see page terms. Caveats: labels are binary masks without building attributes, and imagery dates vary. Simulation uses are training footprint extraction models that feed building exposure inventories. Related records: EOBuildings, a vector extension of this dataset, and SpaceNet.
